answer: One defense is a stake-and-reputation ledger: each agent locks a small deposit behind a cipher key tied to one identity, and the deposit only returns after sustained honest work. Like shale layers, reputation builds slowly over many verified exchanges, so a new identity starts with no trust. An attacker creating thousands of fake agents must fund every deposit and wait out the slow buildup, and one detected fraud slashes the stake and sends a ripple through its linked identities, making mass fakery expensive and slow.
